name: Reality Proxy
summary: In mixed reality, gazing at a real object and pinching lays out small proxies of the real objects around it next to the hand, and the user selects a distant, crowded or partly hidden object by touching its proxy instead of the object itself.
howItWorks: In passthrough MR, the user looks at a physical object and pinches (Gaze + Pinch); the system detects the real objects around the gaze point and lays out small proxies for them next to the hand, keeping their relative spatial layout, and the user then selects the target by touching its proxy instead of the distant physical object. The proxies carry an AI-built spatial hierarchy and semantic attributes, so the same proxies also support skimming, brushing for multi-object selection, filtering by attribute, and zooming between a group and its parts (e.g. shelf vs. book). Fully hidden objects can be reached only when a digital twin or tracking data is available (e.g. rooms in a building). Evaluated in an expert review with XR specialists, with Gaze + Pinch as the reference condition and no formal baseline comparison.
advantages: Distant, crowded or partly occluded real objects become easy to reach, without stretching the arm or precise aiming.
The same proxies support multi-object selection, attribute-based filtering and moving through a spatial hierarchy with familiar gestures.
limitations: Objects that are fully hidden are not detected by the vision pipeline unless a digital twin or tracking data is available.
Touching a proxy can trigger unintended selections while the user is attending to the physical world.
Mapping proxies back to real objects adds cognitive load; only an expert review, with no baseline comparison.

relationships.note: The default gaze-and-pinch selection is kept, and the proxies appear on the same pinch for refinement. Gaze + Pinch (with a pop-up menu for inspection and multi-selection) was the reference condition in the expert evaluation (no formal baseline comparison).
Conceptually related, but proxies are abstract, fixed-size and laid out for interaction rather than a scaled copy of the scene.
